newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end down on worries about consumption.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end down on worries about consumption.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed moderately lower on Tuesday, extending their losses for a third straight session, as the market was still weighed down by worries over Japan's economy and lack of consumption power, brokers said.
The 225-share Nikkei average shed 153.62 points or 0.78 percent to end at 19,514.45. September futures were weaker, losing 350 points to finish at 19,440.
"What is still dragging the market is the unexpectedly fragile consumption shown, as in the car sales data (on Friday)," said Kenzo Doi, strategist at Kokusai Securities Co Ltd.
Toyota's shares ended down 130 yen at 3,160 yen, as sentiment continued to be hurt by the disappointing Japanese domestic car sales in July.
Blue-chip electronics shares fell on profit-taking, brokers said.
Electronics giant Sony Corp slipped 100 yen to 11,900, while TDK Corp dropped 480 yen to 9,820.

"The downside of the yen seems limited and the weighing of Japanese high-tech stocks in portfolios is almost at the upper limit, which means there is not much room for growth," a market analyst at a foreign brokerage said.
"The outlook of the stock market is cloudy and investors are hurrying to take profits," he added.
Meanwhile, some defensive stocks, such as pharmaceuticals, rose as investors bought shares which are largely immune to cyclical economic changes, brokers said.
Shares of Takeda Chemical Industries Ltd rose 40 yen to close at 3,410 yen.
The second section index was down 20.01 points at 1,714.93, with 8.68 million shares traded. The over-the-counter (OTC) index was down 11.21 points at 1,100.10.
